DynaMix frozen evaluation and outcome-blind reference-pool mapping

Exploratory. Same 164 patients as earlier stages (not untouched); session 1 = pretreatment assumed; not a replication of Tolley et al.; not a test of superiority over E01c. Pretrained DynaMix, Remitter: mean AUC 0.490 (95% bootstrap [0.411, 0.570]); repeats 0.453/0.553/0.464. Saved E01c: 0.577. Random-weight models: 0.504, 0.488, 0.459. Triage rule (mean AUC ≥ 0.60, gain ≥ 0.05 over E01c, positive in every repeat): not met. Permutation test (999 permutations, plus-one p): p = 0.560; null 95th percentile 0.593.

Three questions, kept separate

QuestionEvidence in this stageReading
1. Is DynaMix a stable/useful EEG representation? (label-free)Median split-half reliability 0.03 (pretrained) vs 0.02–0.03 (random); ICC across windows 0.01 vs 0.01–0.01Numerically stable to gating noise (replicate r ≥ 0.96) but NOT patient-stable across windows: median split-half reliability of the 10 latent means is at most 0.07; the best feature is pretrained gate entropy (0.31). The summaries mostly describe the window, not a stable person trait. Says nothing about outcome.
2. Does it predict treatment?Pretrained DynaMix, Remitter: mean AUC 0.490 (95% bootstrap [0.411, 0.570]); repeats 0.453/0.553/0.464. Saved E01c: 0.577. Random-weight models: 0.504, 0.488, 0.459. Triage rule (mean AUC ≥ 0.60, gain ≥ 0.05 over E01c, positive in every repeat): not met. Permutation test (999 permutations, plus-one p): p = 0.560; null 95th percentile 0.593.Patient-level out-of-fold; exploratory; cohort previously used; session-1 timing assumed.
3. Is there evidence that pretraining helps?Pretrained minus random A/B/C mean AUC: -0.015 [-0.086, +0.059], +0.002 [-0.074, +0.079], +0.031 [-0.047, +0.108]Three separate random fits shown; no averaging/selection. Pretraining was on simulated dynamical systems, not EEG.

Decision for this stage

The frozen DynaMix extraction does not meet the pre-set triage rule and its permutation test is non-significant; its summaries are not patient-stable across windows, which is a plausible (not demonstrated) explanation. Pretraining shows no detectable benefit over random weights. I do not recommend trying DynaMix variants (other windows, embeddings, hidden states) without a new, stated hypothesis. The reference-pool mapping is feasible and the EC→EO relationship is strongly predictable (largely a shared per-person amplitude level), so any remission test of deviations from it would need to show information beyond that shared level; it was not run.

Overview (three figures)

1. Cleaning diagnostics (v2 fixed)

Under v2, recordings changed: ok -> ok: 316, ok -> ica_failed: 8, too_few_windows -> too_few_windows: 3, ok -> too_few_windows: 1. 15 patients had changed E01 feature availability (14 newly missing at least one feature, 1 newly available; EC status changed in 1, EO in 8); 9 of those are remitters. Patient-level table stays private (outputs/v2/availability_changes_PRIVATE.csv).

For Remitter the E01→E01c AUC change is +0.060 overall, +0.051 [-0.001, +0.104] in the 149 patients with unchanged availability, so the improvement does not hinge on the changed-availability patients; it is concentrated in patients whose features changed more (see figure). This is a conditional descriptive analysis on saved predictions, not causal attribution.

Component evidence (documentation only; cleaning unchanged)

In the 23-recording outcome-blind QC sample v2 removed 46 components; my reconstruction of the ICA application reproduces v2 output exactly (True). Stricter documentation categories (computed from the saved table): 24 eye-locked (≥5 blinks and blink-locked peak/baseline SD ≥ 3, not drift-like), 3 supported only by HEOG correlation (|r| ≥ 0.3), 12 drift-like (low-frequency fraction ≥ 0.95), and 7 with no supporting eye evidence; 11 of 46 components have fewer than 5 detected blinks. The three non-eye-locked groups are unresolved removals (kept as removed, flagged). Components were not classified from maps alone and nothing was altered.

2. Frozen DynaMix specification (DYNAMIX_PROTOCOL.md)

Weights sha256 a10dc3de0f8e1f98…; K = 8 gating-noise replicates (chosen by the pre-set criterion on 13 outcome-blind non-rTMS recordings; criterion met by all four models: False, so the fallback K=8 applied). Windows: 30 s contiguous, up to 4 per recording, never stitched. Embedding run: 1212 (model × recording) tasks, wall 101 min, summed task time 13.4 h, mean 39.8 s per task (K=8; runtime scales ~linearly in K and models). Evaluation run time: Remitter 4 s, Responder 1 s.

4. Reference pool and EC→EO mapping (no outcomes)

Pool: 1023 listed (848 other discovery + 175 workbook-HEALTHY with EC+EO; 1,023 not 1,129 because ADHD-NF/OCD treatment cohorts are excluded); 261 excluded for missing EC/EO features, 0 dropped as exact duplicates, 762 used (610 train / 152 held-out). Ridge alpha 1 (tuned inside training). Held-out mean R² 0.805 (95% [0.765, 0.835]); pooled MSE ratio vs training mean 0.193; 12/12 outputs beat the mean predictor. Shuffled-pair control: mean R² -0.008 (range -0.059 to 0.065). A better-than-mean mapping would show that EC predicts EO within this mixed-diagnosis population; it does not show remission information, which was not scored.

5. Failures, limits, reproduction

  • 8 patient recordings failed ICA (missing); 17 more had no eligible 30-s window; missing conditions were imputed inside training folds.
  • In the seed-budget sample 11 of 24 non-rTMS recordings had no eligible window (many bad blocks), so the sample is 13 recordings; K stability for random models failed only on the two gate features.
  • DynaMix standardizes each series (amplitude discarded), treats channels independently, and was pretrained on simulated dynamical systems; all EEG-specific choices are mine and frozen in DYNAMIX_PROTOCOL.md.
  • Bootstrap intervals are conditional on saved predictions; repeats are not independent patients; cohort previously used.
  • Reference-pool features use only 12 log powers; no remission scoring of the EC→EO extension was run.

Reproduce (from first_tests/): scripts/19_pool_features.py; 20_cleaning_diagnostics.py; 21_dynamix_prepare.py patients|seedsample; 22_dynamix_seed_budget.py; 23_dynamix_embed.py; 24_dynamix_eval.py; 27_dynamix_permutation.py; 25_dynamix_analysis.py; 26_reference_mapping.py; 28_dynamix_report.py.
